Montréal School Hosts Orientation Fair to Help Students Explore Future Pathways

Event Overview

On Thursday, October 29, École secondaire Marie-Anne, part of the Centre de services scolaire de Montréal (CSSDM), held its orientation fair. The event allowed students to meet representatives from various educational institutions and organizations, as reported in a LinkedIn post by Antonino Papalia.

Purpose and Impact

The fair was intended to give students the opportunity to discover training possibilities, explore different career paths, ask questions, and better project themselves into their future. The school's post indicates that supporting success involves broadening horizons, fostering self‑knowledge, and enabling informed choices.

Practical Implications

Participating students can directly interact with educational institutions and organizations, gaining insights into available programs and professional pathways. This interaction supports the school’s goal of helping students make informed decisions about their educational and career trajectories.

What Is Confirmed and What Is Not

The source confirms the date, location, and general purpose of the event, as well as the participation of multiple educational institutions and organizations. It also thanks the contributing partners and staff. Details such as the exact number of attendees, the specific institutions present, or any measurable outcomes are not provided.

How to Verify
